quote: Wanderer, your footsteps are / the road, and nothing more; / wanderer, there is no road, / the road is made by walking.
source: Antonio Machado, Proverbios y cantares XXIX, lines 1 to 4, Poesías completas (1917), English wording attributed to Betty Jean Craige
note: The poem is Machado’s and the Spanish is settled. The English could not be matched to a printed page. This wording travels as Betty Jean Craige’s, but Wikiquote credits Craige with a different rendering using footprints and path. The book year is given as both 1978 and 1979, and page 143 is unconfirmed.

evidence.where: Spanish text confirmed on Wikiquote and on a Center for the Art of Translation worksheet; the English wording traced only to secondary sites, which disagree about it; the 1978 or 1979 Louisiana State University Press page is lending restricted on the Internet Archive and could not be opened
evidence.edition: Selected Poems of Antonio Machado, trans. Betty Jean Craige, Louisiana State University Press, dated 1978 in some citations and 1979 in others
evidence.locator: Proverbios y cantares XXIX, lines 1 to 4; claimed p. 143, unconfirmed

reason: Two materially different English quatrains circulate under Craige’s name, so at least one credit is wrong, and the scan is lending restricted. Shipping a confident translator, year and page here would be the false citation the standard forbids.
